results.title: Baker–Harman: shifted primes with a large prime factor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every integer $a$ and every real $\theta$ with $0 < \theta \le 0.677$ there is a real $\delta$ with $0 < \delta < 1$ such that, for all sufficiently large real $x$, the number of primes $p \le x$ for which the largest prime factor $P(|p + a|)$ of $|p + a|$ exceeds $x^\theta$ is greater than $\delta x / \log x$. Here $P(0) = 0$ and $P(1) = 1$.

results.title: Pollack–Pomerance–Treviño: nonincreasing runs of Euler's function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For real $x$, let $G_\varphi(x)$ be the largest natural number $k$ for which there is a natural number $n \ge 0$ with $n + k \le x$ and $\varphi(n + 1) \ge \varphi(n + 2) \ge \cdots \ge \varphi(n + k)$ (and $0$ if there is no such $k$), where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function. results.title: s-Zumkeller numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $n$ is s-Zumkeller if its proper divisors can be split into two disjoint nonempty sets whose elements have equal sums of squares. Each of the two sums is then $(\sigma_2(n) - n^2)/2$, where $\sigma_2(n)$ is the sum of the squares of the positive divisors of $n$.

results.title: Unitary s-Zumkeller numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $n$ is a unitary s-Zumkeller number when its proper unitary divisors (the unitary divisors of $n$ other than $n$) split into two nonempty disjoint sets $A$ and $B$ with equal sums of squares, $\sum_{d \in A} d^2 = \sum_{d \in B} d^2$.

results.title: $60$ is s-Zumkeller
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The number $60$ is s-Zumkeller: the squares of its proper divisors $1, 2, 5, 30$ sum to $1^2 + 2^2 + 5^2 + 30^2 = 930$, which is half of the sum of the squares of all proper divisors of $60$.

results.title: Criterion for even s-Zumkeller numbers

results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be the golden ratio. For all integers $p, q, r$, the generalized Beatty sequence $V(p, q, r)(n) = p\lfloor n\varphi \rfloor + qn + r$ takes the value $V(p, q, r)(0) = r$ at $n = 0$.

results.title: Generalized Beatty sequence at one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be the golden ratio. For all integers $p, q, r$, the generalized Beatty sequence $V(p, q, r)(n) = p\lfloor n\varphi \rfloor + qn + r$ takes the value $V(p, q, r)(1) = p + q + r$ at $n = 1$, since $\lfloor \varphi \rfloor = 1$.

results.title: The value at one is a term of a generalized Beatty sequence

results.title: The initial term of a generalized Beatty set

results.title: Layman's theorem: the binomial transform preserves the Hankel transform
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every sequence of integers $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$, the Hankel transform of the binomial transform of $a$ equals the Hankel transform of $a$. Here the binomial transform of $a$ is the sequence $b_n = \sum_{i=0}^{n} \binom{n}{i} a_i$, and the Hankel transform of a sequence $c$ is the sequence whose $n$-th term, for $n \ge 0$, is the determinant of the $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ matrix $(c_{i+j})_{0 \le i, j \le n}$.

results.title: Bounded halting of a single-tape machine
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A single-tape Turing machine $M$ halts within $T$ steps on a word $l$ when, started in its initial state with $l$ on the tape and the head on the first letter of $l$ (on a blank if $l$ is empty), it reaches after some $j \le T$ steps a configuration that has no successor.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a single-tape Turing machine $M$, a list $l$ of symbols and numbers $T \le T'$, if $M$ started on $l$ halts within $T$ steps, then $M$ started on $l$ halts within $T'$ steps.

results.summary: Codes for single-tape machines correspond bijectively to transition tables, that is, to lists of rows, each a list of entries that are either empty or a pair of natural numbers: a code corresponds to its table.

results.title: Table lookup of a code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a code $c$ and numbers $q$ and $a$, the lookup of $c$ at state $q$ and symbol $a$ is the entry in row $q$, column $a$ of the table of $c$: either a pair $(q', s)$ of a next state and an action code, or no entry (halt). It is no entry when the table has no row $q$ or that row has no column $a$.

results.title: The machine of a single-tape code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The machine of a code $c$ is the single-tape Turing machine with states and symbols in $\mathbb{N}$ that, in state $q$ reading symbol $a$, halts if the table lookup of $c$ at state $q$ and symbol $a$ has no entry, and otherwise, if the entry is $(q', s)$, enters state $q'$ and does the action coded by $s$: $0$ moves left, $1$ moves right and $a' + 2$ writes $a'$.

results.title: States of a single-tape code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The set of states of a code $c$ is the finite set of natural numbers consisting of the initial state $0$ and every state $q'$ such that some entry of the table of $c$ is a pair $(q', s)$.

results.title: Codes denote finite machines
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decoded machine is supported by the finite set of states of its code.

results.title: Explicit configurations
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A configuration of the simulation consists of a state $q \in \mathbb{N}$, the list of the cells left of the head (nearest first), the symbol in the cell under the head, and the list of the cells right of the head (nearest first); states and symbols are natural numbers.

results.title: Configurations as tuples
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Configurations correspond bijectively to tuples in $\mathbb{N} \times \mathrm{List}(\mathbb{N}) \times \mathbb{N} \times \mathrm{List}(\mathbb{N})$: a configuration corresponds to the tuple of its state, its cells left of the head, its cell under the head and its cells right of the head.

results.title: TM0 configuration of a simulation configuration
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The TM0 configuration of a configuration $k$ of the simulation has the state of $k$, the cell under the head of $k$ as its head cell, and as the halves of its tape left and right of the head the cells of $k$ left and right of the head, nearest first, followed by infinitely many blanks.

results.title: Acting on a configuration
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $k$ be a configuration with left cells $L$ (nearest first), head cell $h$ and right cells $R$ (nearest first), let $q'$ be a state and let $s$ be an action code. Acting on $k$ with $q'$ and $s$ gives a configuration with state $q'$, as follows. For $s = 0$ (move left), its head cell is the first entry of $L$, or the blank $0$ if $L$ is empty, its left cells are $L$ without its first entry, and its right cells…

results.title: Output of a configuration
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The output of a configuration $k$ is the list consisting of the symbol under the head of $k$ followed by the cells right of the head (nearest first), with all trailing blanks $0$ removed.

results.title: Initial configuration of the code simulation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The initial configuration of the simulation on a list of bits $x$ has state $0$, an empty list of cells left of the head, the head on the first symbol of the input word of $x$ (the blank $0$ if $x$ is empty), and the remaining symbols of the input word, in order, right of the head.

results.title: One step of a code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a code $c$ and a configuration $k$ of the simulation, look up the table entry of $c$ at the state of $k$ and the symbol under the head of $k$. If there is no entry, the step is undefined (the machine halts); if the entry is $(q', s)$, the step is the configuration obtained from $k$ by entering the state $q'$ and doing the action coded by $s$.

results.title: One step of a code, or stay when halted
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a code $c$ and a configuration $k$ of the simulation, the configuration after one step of $c$ from $k$ if that step is defined, and $k$ itself if $c$ halts at $k$.

results.title: Clocked configuration of a code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a code $c$, a list of bits $x$ and $T \in \mathbb{N}$, the configuration of $c$ on $x$ after $T$ steps is obtained from the initial configuration on $x$ by applying $T$ times the step of $c$, where a step leaves a halted configuration unchanged. It is the configuration after $T$ steps, or the halting configuration if the machine halts earlier.

results.title: The clocked evaluator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a code $c$, a list of bits $x$ and a clock $T \in \mathbb{N}$, run the simulation of $c$ on $x$ for at most $T$ steps. If it halts within $T$ steps, the result is the output of the halting configuration: the tape from the head rightwards, with trailing blanks dropped. Otherwise there is no result.

results.title: Explicit steps agree with the decoded machine
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every code $c$ and every configuration $k$ of the simulation, the decoded TM0 machine of $c$ halts at the TM0 configuration of $k$ exactly when the step of $c$ from $k$ is undefined, and otherwise its step from the TM0 configuration of $k$ is the TM0 configuration of the step of $c$ from $k$.

results.title: The explicit initial configuration is the machine's
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a list of bits $x$, the initial configuration of the simulation on $x$, read as a configuration of a single-tape machine, is the initial configuration of a single-tape machine on the input word of $x$.

results.title: The output of a configuration as a Mathlib half-tape
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every explicit configuration $k$, the half-tape of the Mathlib configuration of $k$ from the head rightwards (the cell under the head followed by the cells to its right) is the output of $k$, read with blanks beyond its end.

results.title: Iterated steps of the decoded machine
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c$ be a code, $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $k$ an explicit configuration. Run the machine of $c$ for $n$ steps from the Mathlib configuration of $k$, and run the explicit simulation of $c$ for $n$ steps from $k$, where a run that reaches a configuration without a successor before completing $n$ steps has no result. Then the first run has a result exactly when the second does, and its result is the Mathlib…

results.title: Bounded halting of a decoded machine through its simulation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a code $c$, a list of bits $x$ and $T \in \mathbb{N}$, the decoded machine of $c$ halts within $T$ steps on the input word of $x$ if and only if the explicit simulation of $c$, started from the initial configuration on $x$, reaches after some $j \le T$ steps a configuration that has no successor step.

results.title: Definedness of the clocked evaluator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a code $c$, a list of bits $x$ and a clock $T \in \mathbb{N}$, the clocked evaluator of $c$ on $x$ with clock $T$ returns a value if and only if the simulation of $c$ has no step from the configuration after $T$ clocked steps on $x$ (the configuration after $T$ steps, or the halting configuration if the machine halts earlier).

results.title: Clocked halting
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a code $c$, a list of bits $x$ and a clock $T \in \mathbb{N}$, the clocked evaluator of $c$ on $x$ with clock $T$ returns a value if and only if the machine of $c$, started on the input word of $x$, halts within $T$ steps.

results.title: Characterization of clocked results
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a code $c$, a list of bits $x$, a clock $T \in \mathbb{N}$ and a list $l$ of natural numbers, the clocked evaluator returns $l$ on $c$, $x$ and $T$ if and only if the configuration of $c$ after $T$ clocked steps on $x$ has no successor step and its output is $l$.

results.title: Monotonicity of the single-tape clocked evaluator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c$ be a code for a single-tape machine, $x$ a list of bits, $l$ a list of natural numbers and $T \le T'$ natural numbers. If the clocked evaluator returns $l$ on $c$ and $x$ with clock $T$, then it also returns $l$ with clock $T'$.

results.title: Clocked results agree with the machine's semantics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c$ be a code, $x$ a list of bits, $T$ a natural number and $l$ a list of natural numbers. If the clocked evaluator, running $c$ on $x$ for at most $T$ steps, returns $l$, then the decoded machine of $c$, started on the input word of $x$, halts, and the tape from its head rightwards in the halting configuration is $l$ followed by blanks.

results.title: Unclocked halting
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a code $c$ and a list of bits $x$, the machine decoded from $c$ halts on the input word of $x$ if and only if there is a clock $T \in \mathbb{N}$ for which the clocked evaluator of $c$ on $x$ with clock $T$ returns a result.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Universality of codes, for machines that read bit inputs. Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with a finite alphabet $\Gamma$ and a finite set of states that contains the initial state and is closed under the transitions of $M$, and let $\iota$ be an injective map from the bits to $\Gamma$ whose values are not the blank. results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The clocked evaluator is primitive recursive in the code, the input and the clock.

results.title: Splitting a sum over $\alpha^{n+1}$ at the last coordinate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type, $M$ an additive commutative monoid, $n$ a natural number and $f : \alpha^{n+1} \to M$. Then $\sum_{x \in \alpha^{n+1}} f(x) = \sum_{y \in \alpha^n} \sum_{a \in \alpha} f(y_0, \dots, y_{n-1}, a)$, where $y = (y_0, \dots, y_{n-1})$.

results.title: Chain of conditional distributions
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A chain of conditional distributions with values in a type $\alpha$ assigns to every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and every assignment $(x_0, \dots, x_{k-1})$ of values in $\alpha$ to the variables $0, \dots, k - 1$ a finitely supported probability distribution $p_k(\cdot \mid x_0, \dots, x_{k-1})$ on $\alpha$, the conditional distribution of variable $k$ given the earlier ones.

results.title: Joint distribution of a chain
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a chain of conditional distributions with values in a type $\alpha$, write $p_k(\cdot \mid x_0, \dots, x_{k-1})$ for the conditional distribution of variable $k$ given the earlier ones. The joint distribution $P_n : \alpha^n \to \mathbb{R}$ of the first $n$ variables is defined by the chain rule: $P_0 = 1$ and $P_{n+1}(x_0, \dots, x_n) = P_n(x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}) \, p_n(x_n \mid x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$.

results.title: Marginalizing the last variable of a chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c$ be a chain of conditional distributions with values in a finite type $\alpha$, and write $P_k$ for its joint distribution of the first $k$ variables. For every $n$ and every $y = (y_0, \dots, y_{n-1}) \in \alpha^n$, $\sum_{a \in \alpha} P_{n+1}(y_0, \dots, y_{n-1}, a) = P_n(y)$.

results.title: The joint distribution of a chain sums to one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c$ be a chain of conditional distributions with values in a finite type $\alpha$, and write $P_n$ for its joint distribution of the first $n$ variables. For every $n$, $\sum_{x \in \alpha^n} P_n(x) = 1$.

results.title: Conditionals of the joint of a chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c$ be a chain of conditional distributions with values in a type $\alpha$, let $P_m$ be its joint distribution of the first $m$ variables, and let $p_n(\cdot \mid y)$ be its conditional distribution of variable $n$ given values $y \in \alpha^n$ of the earlier ones. For every $n$, every $y \in \alpha^n$ with $P_n(y) \ne 0$ and every $a \in \alpha$, we have $P_{n+1}(y, a) / P_n(y) = p_n(a \mid y)$, where…

results.title: Factorization of the joint of a chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a chain of conditional distributions with values in a type $\alpha$, write $p_k(\cdot \mid x_0, \dots, x_{k-1})$ for the conditional distribution of variable $k$ given the earlier ones and $P_n$ for the joint distribution of the first $n$ variables. Then for every $n$ and every $x \in \alpha^n$ we have $P_n(x) = \prod_{k < n} p_k(x_k \mid x_0, \dots, x_{k-1})$.

results.title: Joint distribution determined by the first conditionals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$. If two chains of conditional distributions $c$ and $c'$ with values in a type $\alpha$ have the same conditional distribution of variable $k$ given the earlier variables for every $k < n$, then they have the same joint distribution of the first $n$ variables.

results.title: Replacing one conditional of a chain
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a chain $c$ of conditional distributions with values in $\alpha$, an index $n$ and a family $f$ assigning to each $y \in \alpha^n$ a probability distribution $f(y)$ on $\alpha$, the updated chain has conditional distribution $f$ for variable $n$ and the same conditional distribution as $c$ for every other variable.

results.title: The chain rule
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite nonempty type and $n \in \mathbb{N}$. For every function $P : \alpha^n \to \mathbb{R}$ with $P(x) \ge 0$ for all $x$ and $\sum_x P(x) = 1$, there is a chain of conditional distributions with values in $\alpha$ whose joint distribution of the first $n$ variables equals $P$.

results.title: Bayesian network
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A Bayesian network with values in a type $\alpha$ on the nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$, listed in a topological order, assigns to each node $k$ a finite set of parents among the earlier nodes $0, \dots, k - 1$, and a conditional probability table: for each assignment of values in $\alpha$ to the parents of $k$, a finitely supported probability distribution on $\alpha$ for the value of node $k$.

results.title: The chain of a Bayesian network
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A Bayesian network $b$ on nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$ with values in a nonempty type $\alpha$ defines a chain of conditional distributions. For $k < n$, the conditional distribution of variable $k$ given values $y_0, \dots, y_{k-1}$ of the earlier variables is the table of node $k$ applied to the values $y_j$ of its parents $j$. For $k \ge n$ it is the point mass at a fixed arbitrary element of $\alpha$.

results.title: Joint distribution of a Bayesian network
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $B$ be a Bayesian network on the nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$ with values in a nonempty type $\alpha$. The joint distribution of $B$ is the function $P : \alpha^n \to \mathbb{R}$ given by $P(x) = P_n(x)$ for $x \in \alpha^n$, where $P_n$ is the joint distribution of the first $n$ variables of the chain of conditional distributions of $B$.

results.title: Factorization of a Bayesian network
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The joint is the product over nodes of the probability of the node's value given the values of its parents.

results.title: The joint distribution of a Bayesian network sums to one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $B$ be a Bayesian network on the nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$ with values in a finite nonempty type $\alpha$, and let $P$ be its joint distribution. Then $\sum_{x \in \alpha^n} P(x) = 1$.

results.title: The effect posterior of the single-effect regression
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The effect posterior of the single-effect regression (Wang et al. 2020): given `y = x β + e` with `β ~ N(0, σ₀²)` independent of `e ~ N(0, σ² I)`, for almost every `y` the effect is normal with mean `σ₀² / (σ₀² + s²) · β̂` and variance `σ₀² s² / (σ₀² + s²)`, where `β̂ = olsEffect x y` and `s² = olsVar σ2 x`.

results.title: The five colocalization hypotheses
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The five coloc hypotheses: no association (`h0`), trait 1 only (`h1`), trait 2 only (`h2`), two distinct causal variants (`h3`), one shared causal variant (`h4`).

results.title: Colocalization hypothesis of a causal configuration
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The hypothesis of a configuration `(causal variant of trait 1, causal variant of trait 2)`, `none` meaning no causal variant.

results.title: Colocalization prior parameters
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Non-negative coloc configuration-weight parameters (Giambartolomei et al. 2014): `p1`, `p2`, `p12` for a variant causal for trait 1 only, trait 2 only, and both. The cited hypothesis weights use null weight `1`. The bound also supports a separate normalized categorical-prior model.

results.title: Null mass of the categorical colocalization prior
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The remaining null mass in the optional normalized categorical-prior model.

results.title: Normalized categorical colocalization prior
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A normalized categorical prior, distinct from the cited coloc relative weights.

results.title: Unnormalized colocalization configuration weight
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The cited coloc unnormalized configuration weight, whose H0 weight is `1`.

results.title: Nonnegativity of categorical configuration priors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Categorical configuration priors are non-negative.

results.title: Nonnegativity of colocalization configuration weights
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Cited coloc configuration weights are non-negative.

results.title: Bayes factor of a colocalization configuration
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Bayes factor of a configuration against the null: the product of the two traits' Bayes factors, `1` for a trait without a causal variant (the two studies are independent).

results.title: Nonnegativity of configuration Bayes factors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A configuration Bayes factor is non-negative when both traits' Bayes factors are.

results.title: Closed-form colocalization hypothesis scores
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The cited coloc closed-form algebraic scores. H0 has score `1`; H1--H4 retain the per-configuration coefficients of Giambartolomei et al. (2014). They are unnormalized hypothesis weights, and hence have a probability interpretation, when the Bayes factors are non-negative.

results.title: Closed-form scores for the categorical colocalization prior
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Closed forms for the optional normalized categorical-prior model. This differs from the cited coloc formula only in using its remaining null mass rather than the cited H0 weight `1`.

results.title: The coloc closed forms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The coloc closed forms (Giambartolomei et al. 2014): the sum of unnormalized configuration weight times Bayes factor over each hypothesis equals its closed form.

results.title: Nonnegativity of closed-form colocalization scores
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Cited coloc closed-form scores are non-negative on the Bayes-factor domain.

results.title: Positivity of colocalization evidence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Cited coloc evidence is strictly positive for non-negative Bayes factors because H0 has unnormalized weight `1`.

results.title: Categorical-prior hypothesis scores equal their closed forms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The corresponding closed forms for the optional normalized categorical-prior model.

results.title: Categorical colocalization priors sum to one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The optional categorical configuration priors sum to one.

results.title: Colocalization normalization identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The unconditional algebraic coloc normalization identity: each hypothesis's configuration score divided by the total score equals its closed-form score divided by the closed-form total. For arbitrary real `bf1` and `bf2` these ratios need not be probabilities. See `colocPosterior_nonneg` and `sum_colocPosterior_eq_one` for the probability-domain results.

results.title: Nonnegativity of colocalization posteriors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Normalized cited coloc hypothesis weights are non-negative for non-negative Bayes factors.

results.title: Colocalization posteriors sum to one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Normalized cited coloc hypothesis weights sum to one for non-negative Bayes factors.

results.title: Posterior identity for the categorical colocalization prior
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The normalized posterior identity for the separate categorical-prior model.

results.title: Credible set of variants
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A `ρ`-credible set: its total posterior inclusion probability is at least `ρ`.

results.title: Prefix of variants in a given order
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The first `k` variants in the order `σ`.

results.title: Cardinality of a sorted prefix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A prefix of length `k ≤ card ι` has `k` elements.

results.title: Sorted prefix carries the most posterior mass
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The `k` largest values carry the most mass: if `σ` sorts `α` in decreasing order, no set of `S.card` variants has more mass than the prefix of that length.

results.title: The shortest credible prefix has minimum size
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The shortest credible prefix has minimum size (Maller et al. 2012; Wang et al. 2020): if `σ` sorts `α` in decreasing order and no prefix shorter than `k` is `ρ`-credible, every `ρ`-credible set has at least `k` elements.

results.title: A minimum-size credible set exists and is a sorted prefix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the total mass is at least `ρ`, some prefix of length `k` is `ρ`-credible, has `k` elements, and every `ρ`-credible set has at least `k` elements.
